html:
David IV, called the Builder, was king of Georgia from 1089 to 1125, who freed the country from the Seljuk Turks and made it the leading power of the Caucasus.

He came to the throne at 16 when the kingdom was a Seljuk tributary. He stopped the tribute, reformed the church, and built a standing army, settling tens of thousands of Kipchak families from the steppe to serve in it. He crushed a large Seljuk coalition at the Battle of Didgori in 1121 and took Tbilisi in 1122. He founded the monastery and academy of Gelati near Kutaisi in 1106, where scholars taught philosophy and theology, and where he is buried. His great granddaughter was Queen Tamar.
sum: David IV, called the Builder, was king of Georgia from 1089 to 1125, who freed the country from the Seljuk Turks and made it the leading power of the Caucasus.
